pages.intent: how many people came, when, and how they got here
pages.message: Visits rose 6.0% to 8.42 million, and more than a third of visitors now arrive without a car

exhibits.reader_must_see: that this year ran above last year in almost every month, and that August is the peak at about three and a half times January
exhibits.comparison: each month this year against the same month last year, and the summer peak against the winter low
exhibits.data: twelve monthly visit counts in thousands for each of two years

forms_considered.form: two-line chart by month
forms_considered.reason: chosen: the seasonal shape and the gap between years read as two lines over one calendar

forms_considered.form: clustered columns by month
forms_considered.reason: twenty-four bars crowd the page and the seasonal shape is lost among them

forms_considered.form: table of twelve months
forms_considered.reason: a general reader would have to compare numbers to see the summer peak

exhibits.why: the reader sees the season as one shape and this year's line sitting on top of last year's without reading a figure
exhibits.marks: this year's line in lake blue and last year's in stone grey, each named in its own colour in the units line like a map key; a value axis in thousands with light gridlines so each month and the gap between years can be read; the August peak ringed in sunset orange and the January low labelled, both in thousands as the units line says

exhibits.reader_must_see: that the share arriving by bus, shuttle or train rose from 19% to 25% while car arrivals fell
exhibits.comparison: each way of arriving this year against last year, as shares of all visits
exhibits.data: three shares for each of two years, each year summing to 100

forms_considered.form: small table of shares with a change column
forms_considered.reason: chosen: six shares and their change read across three short rows

forms_considered.form: two 100% stacked bars
forms_considered.reason: the small walking share has no room for its label, and a change in a middle segment is hard to judge

exhibits.chosen_form: small table of shares with a change column
exhibits.why: the reader looks up their own way of arriving and reads its change directly in points
exhibits.marks: the bus, shuttle and train row in bold with its change in sunset orange, the claim of the title

pages.intent: whether the wildlife and habitats we protect are recovering
pages.message: Six of nine priority species have grown since 2021; three tied to rivers and old pinewood have fallen
pages.deliberate_parallel: the conservation page sets its main exhibit beside a panel of side facts as the visitors page does, so a reader learns where the headline exhibit and the supporting facts sit

exhibits.reader_must_see: which species grew and which fell since the 2021 count, and by how much, with the fallers set apart
exhibits.comparison: each species' change since its 2021 baseline count against no change, and against each other
exhibits.data: nine signed percentage changes, six positive and three negative

forms_considered.form: sorted diverging horizontal bars
forms_considered.reason: chosen: sign and size read as direction and length from one zero line, in rank order

forms_considered.form: table of counts in 2021 and 2025
forms_considered.reason: counts of eagles and mussels are on different scales, so the reader would compute each change

forms_considered.form: status badges for improving, stable and declining
forms_considered.reason: drops the size of each change, which the reader needs to judge how worried to be

exhibits.why: a general reader sees growth to the right in green and decline to the left in red, largest first, without arithmetic
exhibits.marks: values at every bar end; a bracket in sunset orange beside the three fallers saying they are next year's focus

exhibits.reader_must_see: how much habitat we restored this year, against the target, and in which kinds of work
exhibits.comparison: each kind of work's hectares against the year's total, and the total against the 2,000 hectare target
exhibits.data: three areas in hectares, their total and the target

forms_considered.form: small table of hectares and shares with a total row
forms_considered.reason: chosen: three figures and their total read down one column, the share beside each

forms_considered.form: a sentence per kind of work
forms_considered.reason: three lines of prose bury the total and give no share

forms_considered.form: a stacked bar against the target
forms_considered.reason: a second chart beside the species bars would compete with the page's main exhibit for three figures

exhibits.chosen_form: small table of hectares and shares with a total row
exhibits.why: a general reader checks the total against the target and sees that peatland is most of it; a table states both without a second chart
exhibits.marks: the total row bold over a rule; the target stated in the line above

pages.intent: where the money came from and where it went
pages.message: Of every $100 we spent, $32 went to conservation and $10 to running the service

exhibits.reader_must_see: what share of each $100 spent went to each area, conservation first, and how small running the service is
exhibits.comparison: the six spending areas against each other as shares of total spending
exhibits.data: six spending amounts in $m summing to 145.1, expressed as whole dollars of every $100 that sum to 100

forms_considered.form: sorted horizontal bars of every $100 spent
forms_considered.reason: chosen: six shares from 3 to 32 compare as lengths, and long area names sit level beside them

forms_considered.form: doughnut of spending
forms_considered.reason: angles of six slices are hard to compare and the small slices lose their labels

forms_considered.form: single 100% stacked bar
forms_considered.reason: the 3 and 9 segments are too narrow to carry their names

exhibits.chosen_form: sorted horizontal bars of every $100 spent
exhibits.why: dollars of every $100 turn a budget into a count anyone can read, and sorting puts the title's figure first
exhibits.marks: the conservation bar in sunset orange, the rest in lake blue; each bar labelled with its dollars of every $100 and the area's $m in its name

exhibits.reader_must_see: where the $148.3m came from this year beside last year, and that the government grant is about two thirds of it
exhibits.comparison: each source of income this year against last year, and each against the total
exhibits.data: five income sources in $m for two years with totals of 140.8 and 148.3

forms_considered.form: income table with a totals row
forms_considered.reason: chosen: five sources in two years and a total that ties read in one small grid

forms_considered.form: stacked column for each year
forms_considered.reason: the small sources are thin slivers and the reader cannot read their amounts

exhibits.chosen_form: income table with a totals row
exhibits.why: a reader checking the accounts looks figures up and sees them add up to the total
exhibits.marks: the totals row bold over a rule; the government grant row's share stated in the lead-in

pages.intent: how the volunteer programme has grown and what volunteers did
pages.message: Volunteers gave 192,000 hours this year, up 63% in four years

exhibits.reader_must_see: that volunteer hours rose every year for five years, and that the number of volunteers rose with them
exhibits.comparison: each year's hours against the year before, with the volunteer count under each year
exhibits.data: five yearly totals of hours in thousands, and five counts of volunteers

forms_considered.form: column chart of hours with volunteer counts under each year
forms_considered.reason: chosen: the rise reads as heights and the counts sit under the year they belong to

forms_considered.form: two lines on two axes
forms_considered.reason: two scales invite a false reading of where the lines cross

forms_considered.form: table of five years
forms_considered.reason: the reader would compare numbers instead of seeing the steady rise

exhibits.chosen_form: column chart of hours with volunteer counts under each year
exhibits.why: heights show the growth at a glance and the row of counts answers the next question, how many people
exhibits.marks: values on every column; this year's column in sunset orange where the title's figure lands; the volunteer row named at its left

exhibits.reader_must_see: that hours grew because more people volunteered, not because each gave more
exhibits.comparison: hours per volunteer in each of the five years
exhibits.data: five yearly ratios of hours to volunteers, all near 40

forms_considered.form: two-column table of year and hours per volunteer
forms_considered.reason: chosen: five near-equal figures read exactly beside the chart that shows the totals

forms_considered.form: a line of hours per volunteer
forms_considered.reason: a flat line at 40 in a narrow column says less than the figures

exhibits.chosen_form: two-column table of year and hours per volunteer
exhibits.why: a reader of the hours chart asks whether people gave more time or more people came; the ratio answers it
exhibits.marks: none: the figures are close, and that is the point

pages.intent: what we will do next year and how readers can hold us to it
pages.message: Five commitments for 2026-27, costing $13.6m, each with a measure we will report next year

exhibits.reader_must_see: each commitment, what we will do, the measure a reader can check next year, and what it costs
exhibits.comparison: the five commitments against each other by cost, and each against the figure it moves on the earlier pages
exhibits.data: five rows of short sentences with a budget in $m each, totalling 13.6

forms_considered.form: table of commitments with a totals row
forms_considered.reason: chosen: four facts per commitment read across one row, and the costs add to the total

forms_considered.form: five numbered cards in a row
forms_considered.reason: five narrow cards would wrap each sentence into a tall column and hide the costs

exhibits.chosen_form: table of commitments with a totals row
exhibits.why: the reader comes back to this page next year to check each measure, and a table is what they look up
exhibits.marks: the measure column in bold so the promise is what the eye finds; the total bold over a rule
